summary: This work demonstrates continuous-wave microwave-to-optical transduction using a 5 ppm doped Yb:YSO crystal coupled to a 3D loop-gap resonator, achieving an internal efficiency of $2\times10^{-8}$ and 200 kHz bandwidth at zero magnetic field. The measurement establishes strong spin-microwave coupling ($g_{m,\mathrm{ens}}/2\pi = 850$ kHz, $C_m = 2.6$) and projects that optimized parameters (50 ppm doping, reduced beam diameter, increased pump power) could reach $10^{-4}$ efficiency while preserving the long coherence times ($T_{2,\mathrm{o}} = 800$ µs, $T_1 = 1.3$ ms) needed for quantum memory integration.
motivation: Yb:YSO offers zero-first-order Zeeman transitions and hyperfine splittings in the GHz range at zero field, making it compatible with superconducting qubits that suffer decoherence in external magnetic fields, unlike Er$^{3+}$-based transducers. The material's long coherence times already establish it as a leading quantum memory platform, motivating exploration of its potential for transduction to enable integrated memory-transducer nodes.
method: The authors couple a 2.5 $\times$ 2.6 $\times$ 10 mm Yb:YSO crystal to a copper 3D loop-gap microwave resonator (resonance 2625.3 MHz, $Q = 653$) and drive a V-type three-level system with optical pump ($|4_g\rangle \leftrightarrow |1_e\rangle$) and microwave fields ($|1_e\rangle \leftrightarrow |2_e\rangle$ at 2623.3 MHz). They measure heterodyne-detected transduction efficiency across the spin transition and characterize spin-cavity coupling via avoided crossing at varied magnetic field.
result: Transduction efficiency is $2\times10^{-8}$ with 200 kHz bandwidth; avoided crossing reveals $g_{m,\mathrm{ens}}/2\pi = 850$ kHz and $C_m = 2.6$. Saturation power measurements estimate $3.7\times10^{14}$ spins in the optical mode volume with $1.7\times10^{-3}$ to $6.7\times10^{-3}$ population fraction in the excited state. Projected improvements via 50 ppm doping, reduced beam waist (150 µm), higher pump power (10 mW), and optical cavity integration could achieve $\sim10^{-4}$ efficiency.
